facts.statement: Fossils of Aerodactylus scolopaciceps are found exclusively in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, Germany, dating to the late Jurassic Period between 150.8 and 148.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossil remains of this species have been found only in the Solnhofen limestone of Bavaria, Germany, dated to the late Jurassic Period (early Tithonian), about 150.8–148.5 million years ago.

facts.statement: In 2014, Vidovic and Martill described Aerodactylus as a new genus based on six juvenile specimens previously attributed to Pterodactylus.
facts.quote: In 2014, Steven U. Vidovic and David M. Martill re-examined von Meyer and Broili's specimens, along with four others, all juveniles.

facts.statement: The name Aerodactylus means 'wind finger' and was named after the Pokémon Aerodactyl.
facts.quote: The generic name derives from the Greek aero (wind) and dactylus (finger), and was chosen in reference to Aerodactyl, a Pokémon based on an amalgamation of different pterosaur groups.

facts.statement: All six known fossil specimens of Aerodactylus are juveniles, but they all preserve complete skeletons.
facts.quote: Aerodactylus is known from six fossil specimens, and though all of them are juveniles, all preserve complete skeletons.

facts.statement: Aerodactylus skulls were long and narrow, containing approximately 64 teeth that became more crowded near the jaw tips.
facts.quote: The skulls of Aerodactylus were long and narrow with about 64 teeth which were more crowded towards the jaw tips.

facts.statement: Unlike some related pterosaurs, the skull and upper jaw of Aerodactylus curved slightly upward rather than being straight.
facts.quote: Unlike some related species, the skull and upper jaw was curved slightly upward, not straight.

facts.statement: A small, hooked beak was present at the tips of Aerodactylus jaws, with the hooks no larger than the surrounding teeth.
facts.quote: A small, hooked beak was present in the very tips of the jaws, with both upper and lower hook no larger than the teeth that surrounded them.

facts.statement: Aerodactylus had a long neck covered in long, bristle-like pycnofibres.
facts.quote: The neck was long, and covered in long, bristle-like pycnofibres.

facts.statement: One specimen shows a soft tissue crest 44 to 51 mm long and 9.5 mm high extending above the eye and the back half of the nasoantorbital fenestra.
facts.quote: One specimen (MCZ 1505, the counter slab of BSP 1883 XVI 1) shows a roughly triangular soft tissue crest extending upward above the posterior half of the naso-antorbital fenestra and the eye; the crest was 44 to 51 mm long (around 38 to 45% of the total length of the skull) and reached a maximum height of 9.5 mm.

facts.statement: The back of the Aerodactylus skull bore a small, cone-shaped crest or 'lappet' pointing backward.
facts.quote: The back of the skull bore a small crest or "lappet" which pointed backward in a cone-shaped structure.

facts.statement: Aerodactylus had webbing between its fingers and toes, a uropatagium between its feet and tail, and a propatagium between its wrist and shoulder.
facts.quote: The wing membrane extended between the fingers and toes as webbing, and a uropatagium (secondary membrane between the feet and tail) was present, as well as a propatagium (membrane between the wrist and shoulder).

facts.statement: The finger and toe claws of Aerodactylus were covered in keratin sheaths that curved into sharp hooks extending well beyond the bone.
facts.quote: Both the finger and toe claws were covered in keratin sheaths that extended and curved into sharp hooks well beyond their bony cores.

facts.statement: The validity of Aerodactylus is disputed, with some experts suggesting its specimens cannot be distinguished from Pterodactylus.
facts.quote: The validity of Aerodactylus has been disputed, with some pterosaur experts suggesting that none of the specimens referred to this genus are distinguishable from Pterodactylus.

facts.statement: Bennett argued that Aerodactylus is a junior synonym of Pterodactylus because the skull differences are trivial and the specimens represent individual variation rather than a distinct species.
facts.quote: He contended that A. scolopaciceps was named based on skull features that were only trivially different from those of Pterodactylus, that Aerodactylus was founded on an unnatural assemblage of specimens, and that no evidence had been presented to rule out the effects of taphonomy or individual variation.

facts.statement: In 2024, Smyth and Unwin agreed with Bennett, concluding that Aerodactylus scolopaciceps consists of juvenile Pterodactylus antiquus specimens.
facts.quote: Robert S. H. Smyth and David Unwin, in 2024, agreed with his assessment, and concluded that A. scolopaciceps consists of juvenile P. antiquus specimens.

facts.statement: Aerodactylus is classified within the family Aurorazhdarchidae.
facts.quote: familia: Aurorazhdarchidae

facts.statement: Scientists know Aerodactylus from six fossil specimens, all of which are juveniles preserved as complete skeletons.
facts.quote: Aerodactylus es conocido a partir de seis especímenes fósiles, y aunque todos ellos son juveniles, están preservados como esqueletos completos.

facts.statement: Aerodactylus skulls were long and narrow, containing nearly 64 teeth crowded toward the jaw tips.
facts.quote: Los cráneos de Aerodactylus eran largos y estrechos con cerca de 64 dientes los cuales se apiñaban hacia las puntas de las mandíbulas.

facts.statement: A small hooked beak was located at the front of the upper jaws, with the beak parts no larger than the surrounding teeth.
facts.quote: Un pequeño pico ganchudo se encontraba en el extremo frontal de los maxilares, siendo ambas partes del pico no más grandes que los dientes que las rodeaban.

facts.statement: The long neck was covered with long, bristle-like picnofibers.
facts.quote: El cuello era largo, y cubierto con largas picnofibras similares a cerdas.

facts.statement: Specimen MCZ 1505 shows a triangular soft-tissue crest extending over the back half of the nasoantorbital fenestra and eye, measuring 44 to 51 mm long (about 38 to 45% of total skull length) with a maximum height of 9.5 mm.
facts.quote: Un espécimen, MCZ 1505, muestra una cresta de tejido blando más o menos triangular que se extendía hacia arriba sobre la mitad posterior de la fenestra nasoanteorbital y el ojo; la cresta medía de 44 a 51 milímetros de largo (alrededor del 38 a 45% de la longitud total del cráneo) y alcanzaba una altura máxima de 9,5 mm.

facts.statement: A small crest or "ear tuft" pointed backward at the back of the skull, forming a conical structure.
facts.quote: En la parte posterior craneal había una pequeña cresta u "orejera" la cual apuntaba hacia atrás formando una estructura cónica.

facts.statement: The claws on the hands and feet were covered in keratin sheaths that gave them greater length and a hook-like curvature beyond their bone cores.
facts.quote: Las garras de manos y pies estaban igualmente cubiertas de estuches de queratina que les daban mayor longitud y una curvatura a modo de gancho más allá de sus núcleos óseos.

facts.statement: Vidovic and Martill separated P. scolopaciceps from P. kochi, considering it distinct enough to warrant its own genus name, Aerodactylus, derived from the Pokémon Aerodactyl.
facts.quote: Cuando Vidovic y Martill separaron a P. scolopaciceps de P. kochi ellos consideraron que era lo suficientemente distinto como para tener su propio nombre de género al que denominaron Aerodactylus, derivado del Pokémon llamado Aerodactyl.

facts.statement: Aerodactylus belongs to the parent group Aurorazhdarchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Aurorazhdarchidae

facts.statement: Aerodactylus is classified in the family Aurorazhdarchidae.
facts.quote: Family: Aurorazhdarchidae

facts.statement: Aerodactylus is classified as a reptile.
